;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Piracy in the Gulf of Guinea]]
**The [[Bulgarians|Bulgarian]] captain of [[Portugal|Portuguese]]-flagged [[cargo ship]] the ''Tommi Ritscher'', who was [[kidnap]]ped along with seven other sailors by [[pirate]]s off the coast of [[Benin]] last month, is freed. The captain was kidnapped at the port of [[Cotonou]] in the [[Gulf of Guinea]] on April 19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-benin-piracy-bulgaria/kidnapped-captain-of-portugal-flagged-ship-freed-bulgaria-idUSKBN23117U (Reuters)]

*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
**[[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Shinzo Abe]] lifts the [[state of emergency]] in all remaining parts of the country, including [[Tokyo]]. [https://apnews.com/ea1e26e3d06c2c7170cd4e49d0ad1e94 (Associated Press)]

;International relations
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**The Coast Guard of [[Libya]] stops nearly 400 migrants attempting to cross the [[Mediterranean]] in five boats in the past two days, according to the office for migrants of the [[United Nations]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-migrants/libya-stops-nearly-400-migrants-attempting-to-cross-to-europe-iom-idUSKBN2311R6 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*The [[government of Cyprus]] will [[deport]] 17 immigrants suspected of having links to extremist groups or involved in acts of [[terrorism]]. [https://apnews.com/fd68ffed5fef1c5cdf5931ee91cb6899 (AP News)]
*[[Murder of George Floyd]]
**[[George Floyd]] dies after being restrained by [[Minneapolis Police Department|police]] in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]], United States, subsequently [[George Floyd protests|triggering public outrage]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/05/26/us/minneapolis-police-encounter-death-trnd/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Burundian general election]]
**Candidate for the ruling party, [[National Council for the Defense of Democracy – Forces for the Defense of Democracy]], and retired general [[Evariste Ndayishimiye]] wins the election with 68.72% of votes cast amid an election preceded by [[political violence]] including the arrest, [[torture]] and [[murder]] of opposition activists, according to a local [[human rights]] group. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-burundi-election/burundis-ruling-party-wins-presidential-election-idUSKBN2311G5?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Surinamese general election]]
**Citizens of [[Suriname]] head to the polls in the country's latest general election. It is the first election after Suriname's [[President of Suriname|president]] [[Dési Bouterse]] was convicted of murder for the [[December murders]] in 1982. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-52796519 (BBC News)]
